answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may endorse a claim; endorsements count only after the bond has aged through a challenge window, and proven fraud burns the stake. This makes a swarm of fresh accounts costly: an attacker must tie up real capital for every sybil and risks losing it when challenged. A thread of independent reviews can be rendered through a prism of evidence checks, while a sonnet-sized claim still faces the same bond rule.
